A house full of smart things is still a house you have to think about: what did the kids leave on, did the garage ever close, is the heating running for nobody. Flight Check-In

Checked in when the window opens, boarding pass in chat.

Try saying

Check me in

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Flight Check-In

Check-in opens 24 hours before a flight and the good seats are gone in minutes, so the job is really an alarm clock you have to answer. This answers it.

It finds the flight in your inbox, where the airline already sent it: the confirmation code, the name as they spell it, the flight number and the date. When the window opens it goes to the airline's own site in a browser window on your computer, identifies the booking with the code and your surname, works through the questions, takes a seat that costs nothing, and sends you the boarding pass.

It buys nothing. Not a seat, not a bag, not priority boarding. If check-in cannot finish without paying, it stops and tells you what is being asked for and what it costs. It cannot enter card details at all, and the button that takes money comes back to you, which is true of every site your agent uses.

It does not change or cancel bookings either. If the flight is wrong, it says so and leaves it to you.

What Flight Check-In needs

Needs Computer control turned on, which is off until you switch it on. Your agent works the site in a browser window on your own computer, and you can watch it. It never types a password or a card you pay with, and it asks before pressing anything that finalizes.

Home Lights

The lights answer to words instead of to an app.

Try saying

Turn off the desk lampWhat Govee lights do I have?

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Home Lights

Your agent finds the lights on your network, you choose which ones it may touch, and from then on plain words work: "turn off the desk lamp", "dim the bookcase to 30", "make the shelf light warm white". Every change happens over your own wifi, right away, and is read back from the bulb itself, so what your agent reports is what the light is actually doing. "Undo that" works. Finding a Hue bridge asks Philips' own server which bridges are on your network, the way the Hue app does. Your agent knows your lights by the names and rooms you give them, and those reach your AI company like everything else it reads.

Be clear about what this needs, so it never surprises you:

It works with exactly three brands today: Philips Hue (through its own bridge, paired by pressing the bridge's round button), WiZ, and LIFX. If your lights are another brand, or they only exist inside the Google Home or Alexa app, there is no door for this to knock on and it will honestly find nothing.

It reaches lights only while this computer is at home: on, awake, with Archie open, and on the same wifi as the lights. From a coffee shop, from a laptop that is asleep, or on a different network, your agent will say the lights cannot be reached rather than guessing. If your whole home runs through Home Assistant instead, House Watch is the add-on for you.

On a Mac, the first scan makes the computer ask whether Archie may find devices on the local network. Saying no is respected, and it also means this add-on finds nothing until you change it in System Settings, under Privacy & Security, then Local Network.

Works with

  • Hue, WiZ or LIFX on your wifi
  • Govee
  • Lifx

Setting up Home Lights

  1. Nothing to set up for Philips Hue, WiZ and LIFX on your own wifi. Add those on the Home devices card: your agent scans, you pick which ones it may touch.
  2. Govee only: get a key in the Govee Home app, under Settings, Apply for API Key. Paste it in Archie on the Connections tab, then Apps, beside Govee. Generating a new key cancels every older one, so make one and keep it.
  3. LIFX only, and only if you want your lights to answer while this computer is away from home: make a token at cloud.lifx.com/settings and paste it beside LIFX on the same screen. On your own wifi, the Home devices card is faster and needs no token.

Made by Otian AI.

Leave Time

Try saying

When do I need to leave for the dentist?Add twenty minutes there, parking is awful

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Leave Time

Your calendar says "Dentist, 2pm". It does not say where the dentist is, which is why the leave-now alert on your phone has nothing to tell you. This reads the confirmation email, finds the address, keeps it, and then works out what the drive takes with today's traffic on it, so what you get is a time: leave at 1:22. It sets that as a reminder and hands you a link that opens in whichever maps app you use. Where you are leaving from is worked out too, from the thing before it on your calendar, or from home or work depending on the hour, and it always tells you which one it assumed so you can correct it in a line. Addresses it finds once it keeps forever, so the second time you go to that dentist it costs nothing to work out. You need a TomTom key for the traffic, which is free and takes a minute: no credit card, no account to set up.

Works with

  • a calendar
  • an email account
  • Tomtom

Setting up Leave Time

  1. Get a TomTom key, which is free and needs no card. Go to developer.tomtom.com, press Register, confirm your email, and the key is on the dashboard the moment you sign in. Copy it.
  2. In Archie, open the Connections tab, then Apps, find TomTom, and paste the key in.

House Manager

Runs the house in weeks and seasons, not in hours.

Is the plumber sorted?Not yet. Dan said he would call Tuesday. If you would rather not wait on it, I can pull up the two places from your notes and you can book one directly this afternoon. The slow drain is not urgent, but it has been six weeks.

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about House Manager

A house does not run on a to-do list. It runs on cycles. The filter is a quarterly thing, the gutters are an October thing, the dog's pills are a monthly thing, and the only urgent question most mornings is what changed since yesterday. This voice is built for that shape and for the skills that live in it: home maintenance, car upkeep, pets, and plants, packages, meals, groceries, warranties, birthdays.

Its quiet trick is that it remembers what people said they would do. If Dan said he would call the plumber on Tuesday, that is a fact it holds and says once, in the same flat tone it uses for the recycling. Never as an accusation, never as a tally. A household is a group of people, not a project plan, and this voice will not take a side between people who live together.

When the house starts slipping it says so kindly, once, and then names the smallest thing that would turn it around.

House Manager in a conversation

Morning. Anything I need to know?Three things changed overnight. The box was delivered at 6:40 and it is on the porch. The dishwasher's extended warranty ends Friday, so if that door latch is still sticking, this is the week to call. And the furnace filter is the quarterly one, due Saturday. You have a spare 16x25 on the shelf above the washer. Everything else is on its normal cycle. The fig wants water today.Is the plumber sorted?Not yet. Dan said he would call Tuesday. If you would rather not wait on it, I can pull up the two places from your notes and you can book one directly this afternoon. The slow drain is not urgent, but it has been six weeks.I know, I know. I have not done any of it.You have not, and I am only going to say it the once: the kitchen list has not moved in three weeks, and the car inspection is nine days past due. The inspection is the only one with a real cost attached, and it is a twenty-minute walk-in at the place on Cedar. The rest can wait as long as you want it to. Want me to hold Saturday morning for the inspection and put the kitchen list away until then?
